profile.summary: GeNet classifies shotgun metagenomic reads from raw DNA, without a similarity search against a reference database. It is a convolutional network: the bases of a read are embedded along with their positions, a ResNet style encoder reads them, and the output layers predict several taxonomic ranks at once, each rank's prediction able to see the one above it. The authors also use the network as a feature extractor, reporting that a linear model on top of its representations works for pathogen detection.

summary_quotes.text: We introduce GeNet, a method for shotgun metagenomic classification from raw DNA sequences that exploits the known hierarchical structure between labels for training.
Genet is a convolutional model for shotgun metagenomic classification.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: A read is turned into two embeddings, one for the base and one for its position, over a vocabulary of six symbols, and a one hot encoding is also built. A convolutional encoder follows, made of ResNet blocks that downsample when the block changes and double the filter count, with the number of blocks, the filter count and the filter size set by command line flags. The taxonomy is the part that distinguishes the method: the output has one group of units per rank and, with connect_softmax set, the softmax activations of the higher rank are fed into the next, so the hierarchy between labels is used during training. Class weights per rank are applied through a one hot mask over the units of that rank.

sections.title: Training configuration and data
sections.body: The defaults in the training script are one ResNet block, 128 filters in the first convolution, a filter size of 3 in the row dimension, 1024 fully connected units, a batch size of 64, a read length of 10000, an initial learning rate of 1.0 and a simulated quality score of 15. The flag help gives the acceptance probability as 10 to the power minus the score over ten, while the code computes one minus that value. The configuration also fixes a vocabulary of 6 and an output vocabulary of 100. The repository ships the NCBI taxonomy nodes file and three id lists, for the training microbes, the full set and a pathogen set, and the README says the first run downloads the required genomes from NCBI.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: There is one code release and no published weights: training writes its own weights and tensorboard log into GeNet/saved_models. The repository has no licence file and the GitHub API returns a null licence field. A result must name the flags, because the architecture is built from them, and the id list used, since the training set is the csv file named by dataset_list. The sources read give no model card, no release tag and no checkpoint download. A third party benchmark, the MetageNN paper, reports retraining GeNet and extending its capacity to match their own model, so figures attributed to GeNet elsewhere may refer to that extended version rather than to the published configuration.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Supervised convolutional classifier for shotgun metagenomic reads, predicting several taxonomic ranks at once from raw DNA.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Base and positional embeddings over a vocabulary of 6, then a ResNet style convolutional encoder whose blocks downsample and double the filters, then one output group per taxonomic rank with the higher rank's softmax optionally fed into the next. Defaults: 1 ResNet block, 128 first layer filters, filter size 3, 1024 fully connected units.

strengths.text: It uses the taxonomy during training rather than treating labels as flat, and the code exposes that as a switch: the higher rank's softmax can be connected to the next rank's output group.

quotes.text: exploits the known hierarchical structure between labels for training

strengths.text: The authors report competitive precision and good recall against Kraken and Centrifuge with orders of magnitude less memory, on datasets where a distribution shift occurs. These are their own claims in the abstract.

quotes.text: We show that GeNet obtains competitive precision and good recall, with orders of magnitude less memory requirements.

strengths.text: Its representations are reusable: the authors report over 90 per cent accuracy in a pathogen detection problem from a linear model on top of the learned features, and the repository ships the pathogen id list.

run_guide.summary: Install the environment, extract the shipped NCBI taxonomy, and start a GeNet training run, which downloads its genomes on the first execution.
prerequisites: Anaconda, as the README specifies, and the environment.yml in the repository, which install_requirements.sh uses to create the genet environment.
A GPU: the training script takes a GPU count and defaults to 1.
Network access and disk space for the genomes the first run downloads from NCBI.
The code is TensorFlow 1 era and no licence is declared for it.

steps.title: Get the code and install the dependencies
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/mrojascarulla/GeNet.git
cd GeNet
git checkout --detach aeafc6557f68081f850947b19bffc13fb028701f
bash install_requirements.sh

notes: The record's existing source is the MetageNN paper, which used GeNet as a baseline. That paper was fetched here and is cited only for statements about GeNet, attributed to its authors: the approximately 17 million trainable parameter figure, and their statement that they extended GeNet's capacity to match MetageNN, which leaves it unclear which configuration the figure describes. GeNet's own sources are the repository mrojascarulla/GeNet, taken as official because the README cites arXiv 1901.11015 and mrojascarulla matches the first author, Mateo Rojas-Carulla, and the arXiv abstract page. Coverage is limited because only the abstract of GeNet's own paper was read; the PDF was not saved, since quotes must come from text files. The record description calls GeNet a ResNet classifier with one-hot and positional embeddings of a fixed-length read, which the code supports. No licence is declared and no weights are published. The context_length of 10000 in the structured row is the training default read length, which also sets the positional embedding size, not a measured maximum.
